editorial.purpose: Human-authored headlines only — articles, takes, ranking titles. Signals judgment.

display.purpose: Page hero titles and major section heads.

title.purpose: Card titles, story headlines, athlete names in ranking rows.

label.purpose: Eyebrows, category tags, table headers, stat captions. Wide tracking makes small text read as deliberate.

shadows.name: hover-lift
shadows.purpose: Hover state on interactive cards that navigate. Never a resting state.

shadows.name: overlay
shadows.purpose: Modals, dropdowns, search overlay, site gate — surfaces that genuinely float.

motion.name: ease-standard
motion.purpose: Default easing for state and page transitions.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The single call-to-action style. Signal Orange fill, uppercase label type.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { background: #FF5200; color: #fff; height: 40px; padding: 0 18px; border: none; border-radius: 10px; font-family: 'Lota Grotesque', sans-serif; font-size: 11px; font-weight: 800; letter-spacing: 0.12em; text-transform: uppercase; cursor: pointer; transition: background 0.15s cubic-bezier(0.2,0,0.2,1); } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: #E04600; } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #FF5200; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Ghost Button
components.description: Secondary and toolbar actions. Transparent at rest, fills to Press Gray on hover.
components.css: .ds-btn-ghost { background: transparent; color: #111111; height: 40px; padding: 0 18px; border: 1px solid #ECECEC; border-radius: 10px; font-family: 'Lota Grotesque', sans-serif; font-size: 13px; font-weight: 700; cursor: pointer; transition: background 0.15s cubic-bezier(0.2,0,0.2,1); } .ds-btn-ghost:hover { background: #F5F6F8; } .ds-btn-ghost:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #FF5200; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Category Chip
components.description: Story category eyebrow. Tint fill keeps it subordinate to the headline.
components.css: .ds-chip { display: inline-block; background: #FFF0E9; color: #FF5200; border-radius: 999px; padding: 4px 10px; font-family: 'Lota Grotesque', sans-serif; font-size: 11px; font-weight: 800; letter-spacing: 0.12em; text-transform: uppercase; }

components.name: Content Card
components.description: Flat at rest, hairline border, hover lift only when it navigates.
components.html:
Upcoming Meets
Lausanne Diamond League
components.css: .ds-card { background: #FFFFFF; color: #111111; border: 1px solid #ECECEC; border-radius: 16px; overflow: hidden; transition: box-shadow 0.15s cubic-bezier(0.2,0,0.2,1); } .ds-card:hover { box-shadow: 0 8px 24px rgba(0,0,0,0.08); } .ds-card-hd { padding: 14px 16px; border-bottom: 1px solid #ECECEC; font-family: 'Lota Grotesque', sans-serif; font-size: 11px; font-weight: 800; letter-spacing: 0.12em; text-transform: uppercase; } .ds-card-bd { padding: 24px; font-family: 'Lota Grotesque', sans-serif; font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.5; }

components.name: Search Field
components.description: Primary navigation affordance in the top bar — a wide pill, not an icon button.
components.css: .ds-search { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 10px; background: #FFFFFF; border: 1px solid #ECECEC; border-radius: 999px; height: 44px; padding: 0 16px; color: #6B6F76; transition: border-color 0.15s, box-shadow 0.15s; } .ds-search:focus-within { border-color: #FF5200; box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px #FFF0E9; } .ds-search input { border: none; outline: none; background: transparent; flex: 1; font-family: 'Lota Grotesque', sans-serif; font-size: 15px; color: #111111; } .ds-search input::placeholder { color: #6B6F76; }

components.name: Ranking Row
components.description: Signature component. Oversized numeral, athlete photo, name, and the mandatory editorial bite.
components.html: 1Cole HockerOlympic champion with a kick that ends races in the last 100 meters.
components.css: .ds-rank-row { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 54px 56px 1fr; align-items: center; gap: 16px; padding: 18px 4px; border-bottom: 1px solid #ECECEC; text-decoration: none; color: #111111; cursor: pointer; transition: background 0.15s; } .ds-rank-row:hover { background: #F5F6F8; } .ds-rank-num { font-family: 'Lota Grotesque', sans-serif; font-size: 34px; font-weight: 800; line-height: 1; letter-spacing: -0.04em; text-align: center; } .ds-rank-row--podium .ds-rank-num { color: #FF5200; } .ds-rank-ava { width: 56px; height: 56px; border-radius: 3px; background: #15151a; } .ds-rank-name { display: block; font-family: 'Lota Grotesque', sans-serif; font-size: 17px; font-weight: 800; letter-spacing: -0.01em; } .ds-rank-bite { display: block; margin-top: 3px; font-family: 'Lota Grotesque', sans-serif; font-size: 13.5px; line-height: 1.4; color: #6B6F76; }

components.name: Editorial Lead
components.description: The homepage front door — custom graphic with serif headline. Graphic is the loudest element; chrome stays quiet.
components.html: OpinionHow to DisappearThe strange case of Jonah Koech and track's transparency problemBy Tate Sheehy · 5 min read
components.css: .ds-lead { display: block; text-decoration: none; color: #111111; } .ds-lead-media { display: block; aspect-ratio: 16/9; border-radius: 4px; background: linear-gradient(135deg, #1d4ed8, #0a0a0b); } .ds-lead-body { display: block; padding-top: 16px; } .ds-chip-solid { display: inline-block; background: #B91C3C; color: #fff; border-radius: 4px; padding: 4px 10px; font-family: 'Lota Grotesque', sans-serif; font-size: 11px; font-weight: 800; letter-spacing: 0.12em; text-transform: uppercase; } .ds-lead-title { display: block; margin-top: 12px; font-family: 'Source Serif 4', Georgia, serif; font-size: clamp(30px, 4vw, 46px); font-weight: 600; line-height: 1.06; letter-spacing: -0.02em; } .ds-lead-dek { display: block; margin-top: 10px; font-family: 'Lota Grotesque', sans-serif; font-size: 18px; line-height: 1.4; color: #6B6F76; } .ds-lead-by { display: block; margin-top: 12px; font-family: 'Lota Grotesque', sans-serif; font-size: 13px; color: #6B6F76; }

components.name: Data Table
components.description: The one surface where filled headers and zebra rules are both used — density earns it.
components.css: .ds-table { width: 100%; border-collapse: collapse; font-family: 'Lota Grotesque', sans-serif; } .ds-table th { background: #F7F8FA; color: #6B6F76; text-align: left; padding: 10px 14px; font-size: 11px; font-weight: 800; letter-spacing: 0.12em; text-transform: uppercase; border-bottom: 1px solid #ECECEC; } .ds-table td { padding: 12px 14px; font-size: 14px; border-bottom: 1px solid #F2F2F2; } .ds-table td:last-child { text-align: right; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; font-weight: 700; } .ds-table tbody tr:nth-child(even) { background: #F7F8FA; }

narrative.overview:
StatTC is designed as a working writer's vantage point on the sport. A press box is authoritative without being ceremonial: it exists so someone with a good eye can watch, judge, and file. Everything in it earns its spot — the sightline, the monitor, the stat sheet at your elbow. Nothing is there to impress a visitor.

That translates to an interface where the writing leads and the data sits within arm's reach. A signed take is the front door; rankings are the recurring franchise; the numbers are receipts you reach for mid-argument, never a wall you stare at. The visual language is quiet, high-contrast, and unfussy so the two things that are genuinely StatTC's own — the voice and the custom graphics — are the only elements doing loud work. One orange accent carries every moment of emphasis on the site; when everything can be highlighted, nothing is.

The system is deliberately restrained at the chrome level so it can be generous at the content level. A hand-made athlete graphic should be the most visually interesting thing in any viewport it appears in. If the interface is competing with it, the interface is wrong.
keyCharacteristics: Editorial-first: serif headlines mark authored judgment; sans-serif marks product chrome
Flat surfaces, separated by rules and whitespace rather than shadow
Exactly one accent color, used sparingly enough to still mean something
Data rendered as evidence inside arguments, not as dashboards
Custom graphics are the visual payload; the frame stays out of their way

rules.name: The One Voice Rule
rules.body: Signal Orange is the only accent in the system. Any new hue introduced for decoration — a second 'category color,' a blue gradient, a green trend line — is a defect. Status colors are the sole exception and they may only communicate state, never brand.

rules.name: The Token Rule
rules.body: Every color in a component references a custom property from :root in base.css. A raw hex in a page stylesheet is drift, not a decision.

rules.name: The Serif Means Judgment Rule
rules.body: Source Serif 4 appears only on human-authored headlines — articles, takes, ranking titles. It never appears on navigation, buttons, table headers, or data labels. If a serif headline sits above auto-generated content, either the content needs a human take or the headline needs to be sans.

rules.name: The Two Families Rule
rules.body: Two typefaces, no third. New fonts do not get introduced for a single surface.

rules.name: The Two Breakpoints Rule
rules.body: 960px for structural reflow, 640px for phone density. Every new rule uses the two canonical breakpoints, and stray ones are consolidated on sight.

rules.name: The Lead Is The Front Door Rule
rules.body: On the homepage, the lead story renders above the column split at every viewport width. No schedule module, promo, or data panel may render above it on any screen size.

rules.name: The Flat-At-Rest Rule
rules.body: --shadow-card is legacy and should resolve to none for idle surfaces. If a surface needs separation, use a 1px solid var(--border) rule or a background step to Press Gray — not a shadow.

rules.name: The Radius Means Class Rule
rules.body: Never invent a radius. If an element doesn't map to button/input/card/feature/pill, it needs to be reclassified, not given a new number.

dos: Do resolve every color, radius, and spacing value to a :root custom property from base.css.
Do use exactly two breakpoints — 960px for structural reflow, 640px for phone density.
Do reserve Source Serif 4 for human-authored headlines, so the serif always signals judgment.
Do keep surfaces flat at rest and reach for a hairline rule or background step before a shadow.
Do give every ranking row an editorial bite; if there's no take, render a table instead.
Do let custom graphics be the loudest element in their viewport, and keep surrounding chrome quiet.
Do pair every focus state with a visible indicator that meets WCAG AA contrast.
donts: Don't introduce a second accent color. One orange, plus status colors that may only report state.
Don't write a raw hex in a page stylesheet.

Don't create another bespoke button or card class. The codebase carries 47 distinct button classes and 119 card classes across 13,573 lines of CSS; every new surface must compose the shared primitives.
Don't put a resting shadow on an idle surface.
Don't invent a radius outside the button/input/card/feature/pill scale.
Don't render a stats wall, leaderboard grid, or tool directory on the homepage — data lives on rankings, profiles, and H2H.
Don't let any module render above the lead story on the homepage at any viewport width.
Don't let article prose run the full container width; cap the measure at 65–75ch.
